skill.name: taiwan-oil-price
skill.description: 台灣中油油價查詢——92/95/98 無鉛汽油與超級柴油的每週牌價（官方 open data JSON）與近 7 週歷史。油價、汽油多少錢、柴油價格、加油、下週油價的問題適用。免 API 金鑰、免登入。即時國際油價、預測漲跌、加油站個別售價不適用。
skill.summary: Retrieve official Taiwan CPC fuel prices, effective dates, and approximately seven weeks of price history without authentication.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: Markdown formatting, public CPC URLs, Python HTML decoding, and readable multilingual text explain 18 false positives. Four temporary-file findings expose overwrite or data-tampering risks through predictable shared paths. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Downloads write to predictable shared temporary files, which can follow attacker-created symlinks or collide with concurrent runs.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mktemp -d, download inside it, and remove it after processing.

remediation.issue: Parsers trust predictable shared files that another local process may replace or modify.
remediation.suggestion: Read only files from the same private temporary directory, or pass downloaded data directly to parsers without shared intermediate files.

content.value_statement: Fuel price announcements can differ from prices currently in effect. This skill retrieves official CPC prices and recent history with clear effective dates and units.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve official CPC retail prices for 92, 95, and 98 unleaded gasoline and premium diesel without an API key.
Distinguish currently effective prices from announced next-week prices using their effective dates.
Convert ROC calendar dates to Gregorian dates by adding 1911 to the year.
Extract approximately seven weeks of gasoline and diesel prices from the official CPC history page.
Use the history page when the open-data endpoint fails, and report unavailable data when both sources fail.
Filter other product categories in the same dataset and report their stated pricing units.
limitations: Requires network access and tools such as curl, jq, and Python to follow the documented workflow.
Does not provide live international oil prices, unpublished price forecasts, or individual station selling prices.
History is limited to approximately seven weeks; older records require queries outside this skill.
CPC website changes can break historical parsing, and the documented shared temporary paths need security hardening.

use_cases.title: Check Published Pump Prices
use_cases.description: Retrieve CPC gasoline and diesel list prices with effective dates before planning a fuel purchase.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Fuel Costs
use_cases.description: Compare recent weekly premium diesel list prices for transport cost planning.

use_cases.title: Prepare Price Updates
use_cases.description: Summarize official weekly announcements and distinguish future effective dates from prices already in effect.

prompt_templates.title: Check Gasoline Prices
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the latest official CPC prices for 92, 95, and 98 gasoline. Include units and the effective date.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve a basic price list.

prompt_templates.title: Check Next Week's Announcement
prompt_templates.prompt: Has CPC announced next week's prices? Separate announced prices from currently effective prices, and do not forecast unpublished changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Weekly Diesel Prices
prompt_templates.prompt: Show available premium diesel prices for approximately seven recent weeks. Convert ROC dates and calculate consecutive weekly changes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Sources and Fallbacks
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve CPC retail fuel prices and effective dates. Use private temporary files and the history fallback if needed. Report source failures without inventing values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: handle source failures and safer file processing.

output_examples.input: Show an example CPC fuel price report with an effective date.
output: Illustrative historical example from the skill documentation, not a live lookup.

output_examples.input: If prices retrieved on Sunday take effect on Monday, are they already current?
output: The retrieved prices are announced prices for Monday, not prices already in effect on Sunday.
Use the previous effective price record for Sunday and label Monday's prices with their effective date.

output_examples.input: Both official sources failed. What are the latest prices?
output_examples.output: Current prices could not be verified because both official sources failed. No price figures are reported.

best_practices: Include the source, effective date, currency, and pricing unit with every price report.
Check effective dates before calling an announcement the current price, and convert ROC dates explicitly.
Use private temporary files, check retrieval success, and report source failures without substituting unsupported values.
anti_patterns: Presenting the documentation's historical sample prices as a current lookup.
Predicting unpublished prices or treating future effective prices as already active.
Mixing CPC list prices with station discounts, other suppliers, or incompatible pricing units.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or login?
faq.answer: No. The documented CPC open-data endpoint and public history page require neither.

faq.question: Which fuels are covered?
faq.answer: The main workflow covers 92, 95, and 98 unleaded gasoline and premium diesel. Other dataset categories require separate filtering and unit checks.

faq.question: Can it tell me next week's prices?
faq.answer: Yes, after CPC publishes the announcement. It uses the effective date to identify next-week prices and does not predict unpublished changes.

faq.question: How much price history is available?
faq.answer: The documented history page exposes approximately seven recent weeks. Older records require additional queries outside this skill.

faq.question: What happens when a source fails?
faq.answer: The workflow falls back from open data to the history page. If both sources fail, it reports unavailable data without inventing prices.

faq.question: Are these individual station prices?
faq.answer: No. These are CPC published list prices, not station discounts or Formosa Petrochemical prices.
